newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says to invite bids for 150,000T corn.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says to invite bids for 150,000T corn.

text.p: The state-agency National Food Authority (NFA) may likely invite traders to give price quotes for 150,000 tonnes of corn starting next week, a senior government official told Reuters on Friday.
"We may start inviting suppliers to give their price quotes next week following the approval by President Fidel Ramos of the corn importation," the official said.

Ramos approved the request of Agriculture secretary Salvador Escudero to import tax and duty free 150,000 tonnes of corn to forestall any possible increase in livestock and poultry products this Christmas, the presidential palace said in a statement.

"With the forthcoming Christmas season, the demand for meat and poultry products is expected to rise. Consumers should be given the opportunity to avail of these products at affordable prices," Escudero told Ramos, the statement said.
Philippine feed millers said they have asked the government to import cheaper and better quality corn to bring down prices of local meat products.
Escudero said 10 percent of the proposed imports are scheduled to arrive between November this year and February next year.
"Escudero proposed the importation upon the request of the corn users, namely feedmillers, livestock and poultry raisers..," the palace statement said.
The NFA had imported since the start of the year 250,000 tonnes of corn from the United States and Argentina due to high demand of commodity for animal feed.
